# dsh-docchain
English | 中文
A DSH knowledge base and document conversion plugin bundling filename/content/metadata search, topic
listing, bulk document upload, document-to-Markdown conversion, a multi-subagent deep-research work
flow, and a knowledge-graph (Neo4j) layer — ontology inspection, read-only Cypher, and node/relation
writes all go through the DocChain API (no Neo4j password needed): install once with `plugin_manage
r install_bundle` and it works on any machine — no manual copying into `~/.agents/skills` required.
and it works on any machine — no manual copying into `~/.agents/skills` required. Built on docchain.
Its configuration page goes beyond a single endpoint: it keeps a list of **saved environments** — ea
ch with its own address and its own credential — switches between them in one click, and pre-selects
**topics** per environment, so a later request can say "search this topic" without naming an id.
Apart from `deep-research-advanced` (a pure instruction workflow with no script), every capability i
s also exposed as a **native tool**, executed in-process by the host instead of by shelling out to a
xposed as a **native tool**, executed in-process by the host instead of by shelling out to a script:
| Tool | What it does |
| `docchain_doc_search` | Locate documents by doc_id / document-name keyword, list details, optional

ly read content (paged, resumable) |
| `docchain_content_search` | Search document content by keywor

d; returns matching line numbers and content |
| `docchain_filename_search` | Find documents whose f

ilename matches keywords, within the given topics |
| `docchain_topic_info` | List topics with pagin

ation and a name-or-id keyword filter |
| `docchain_meta_search` | Filter documents by custom metada

ta fields (string/number/time, AND / OR groups) |
| `docchain_upload` | Upload a file, or a folder's

top-level files, to a topic |

The same package installs into either profile — pick the one that matches how you run DSH:
| How you run DSH | Command |

| Desktop app | `dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:wct-lab/dsh-docchain` |
| `dsh web` | `dsh
plugin --profile web add github:wct-lab/dsh-docchain` |

## Configuration (required)
No credentials ship in this package. Every script except `doc2markdown` (Node.js) needs a docchain s
ervice endpoint and an API key before it can run; `doc2markdown` (Node.js) works with neither — it f
alls back to the built-in default endpoint and uploads anonymously, while the same config chain can
point it at a custom endpoint/key.
| Field | Meaning | Required |

| `docchain_url` | docchain service address, e.g. `http://<host>:7100/llmdoc` | Yes |
| `docchain_ap
i_key` | API authentication key | Yes |
Four ways to provide them, in **priority order** (higher wins):

1. Environment variables `DOCCHAIN_URL` and `DOCCHAIN_API_KEY`;
2. per-skill config file `<skill>/sc

ripts/config.json`;
3. the plugin state file `~/.dsh/storages/docchain-config.json` (written by the

plugin config — see below);
4. package-level `skills/docchain_config.json` (file-drop distribution f
allback; the package ships only `docchain_config.example.json` as a template).
Environment variables outrank everything below them, including the environment selected on the plugi
n's configuration page — see Switching between environments.

All scripts need only Node.js. Invoke them from the skill's base directory as `node scripts/<script>
.js …` (see each SKILL.md for parameters).
## Plugin configuration (recommended)
The plugin ships a **configuration page** in the web client: in `dsh web`, open **Plugins** in the s
idebar, find the `dsh-docchain` plugin, and use the configure control on its row. The page manages a
list of environments; an address and a key are properties of an environment, so they are entered an
d edited inside its row — there are no separate top-level fields. The key itself goes to the credent
ial store and is write-only: the page never echoes a stored value, only whether one is set.
The plugin follows the official credential pattern. Its Config schema declares:
| Field | Meaning |
| `docchain_url` | Service endpoint used when no environment is active; volatile, kept in sync with

the active environment by the page |
| `docchain_api_key_ref` | Credential reference name for the ke

y; default `DOCCHAIN_API_KEY` |
| `docchain_api_key` | Fallback literal key (not recommended; the st

ore wins over it) |
| `docchain_environments` | Saved environments (JSON): per entry a name, URL, cr

edential reference and its pre-selected topics; the active entry outranks `docchain_url` |
| `neo4j_
uri` | Neo4j Bolt endpoint, e.g. `neo4j://<host>:17687`; kept for future direct graph tools (current

kept for future direct graph tools (all graph tools currently use the API) |
| `neo4j_database` | N
eo4j database name, default `neo4j` |
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
The bundle inserts one Host plugin (`dsh-docchain`). At activation it registers a skill provider on
`ctx.skills` that serves every `<skills>/<name>/SKILL.md` directory in this package:
- Catalog entries come from each SKILL.md frontmatter (`name`, `description`); bodies are re-read on

every load.
- The provider rank is **450** — project roots (`.dsh/skills` = 100, project `.agents/s
kills` = 200), runtime registrations (250) and `customSkillDirs` (300) keep precedence, as does `~/.
dsh/skills` (400); the bundle outranks `~/.agents/skills` (500) and the bundled root (600). In pract
ice: same-name copies in `~/.agents/skills` are shadowed by this bundle; delete them there if you wa

nt a single source.
- Two optional services carry the configuration page: the host registers `GET /p
lugin/dsh-docchain/topics` on the web server (the browser never holds the API key, so the host queri
es the active environment on its behalf), and a prompt section that describes the active environment
and its selected topics. A profile without those services still gets the skill provider and the pro

jection file.
- Neither the topic route nor the prompt section caches state of its own: both read th
e live row config on every call, so switching an environment or a topic reaches the scripts and the
next model step without a restart.
